rule: D7 lists 'wrong arm' as a fidelity case beside 'wrong count' and 'invented check'. Its binding rule speaks of names bound to the FINDING (plugin / cell / formKey) and of checks and arms 'outside the plan'. A wrong-arm attribution to an arm inside the plan is the case the acceptance table needs refused (an answer that moves a regression to another arm is a fidelity failure), so the oracle reads the finding's armId as one of its bound names: an answer naming a different arm is refused with an arm rule. Fable rules if the implementation reads D7's letter instead; the oracle is not re-based silently.
